questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.explanation: Pierre de Coubertin, who founded the modern Games, designed the rings in 1913.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 2012 Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: London became the first city to host the Summer Olympics three times, after 1908 and 1948.

questions.question: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: It will be LA's third Summer Games, after 1932 and 1984; Brisbane hosts in 2032.

questions.question: Which country did the sprinter Usain Bolt run for?
questions.explanation: Bolt ran the 100 metres in 9.58 seconds in Berlin in 2009.

questions.question: Months before each Olympics, how is the Olympic flame lit at Olympia in Greece?
options: By the Sun's rays, using a curved mirror
With a match from the last host city
questions.answer: By the Sun's rays, using a curved mirror
questions.explanation: The mirror focuses sunlight onto a torch until it bursts into flame.

questions.question: In which sport did Tom Daley win Olympic gold at the Tokyo Games?
questions.explanation: He won the synchronised 10m platform with Matty Lee, then knitted a little pouch to keep his medal in.

questions.question: The Paris 2024 medals each had a small piece of iron from which famous landmark?
questions.explanation: The iron had been removed from the tower during repairs and was cut into hexagons, the shape of France.

questions.question: In which Olympic sport would you use a pommel horse?
questions.explanation: Despite the name there is no horse at all, just a padded box with two handles on top.

questions.question: Which sport, with dancers called B-boys and B-girls, joined the Olympics at Paris 2024?
questions.explanation: Breaking is a style of street dance that began in New York in the 1970s.

questions.question: How long is an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.explanation: That means a 100m race is exactly one length there and back.

questions.question: By the end of the Paris 2024 Games, who had won the most Olympic medals in history?
questions.explanation: The American swimmer won 28 medals, 23 of them gold.

questions.question: In which Paralympic sport do players wear eye shades and throw a ball with bells inside?
questions.explanation: The crowd has to stay silent during play so the players can hear the ball coming.

questions.question: The Paralympic movement began in 1948 with an archery contest at which English hospital?
questions.explanation: Dr Ludwig Guttmann held it for injured ex-service men and women on the day the 1948 London Olympics opened.

questions.question: Which British athlete won gold in the heptathlon at London 2012?
questions.explanation: On 'Super Saturday' Ennis, Greg Rutherford and Mo Farah all won gold within about 45 minutes.

questions.question: To the nearest mile, how long is an Olympic marathon?
questions.explanation: The odd distance of 26.2 miles comes from the 1908 London Games, when the race started at Windsor Castle.

questions.question: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games, in 1896?
questions.explanation: Around 240 athletes took part, all of them men.

questions.question: Sir Steve Redgrave won gold at five Olympics in a row in which sport?
questions.explanation: His golds came at every Games from Los Angeles 1984 to Sydney 2000.

questions.question: In which event would an athlete perform the 'Fosbury Flop'?
questions.explanation: Dick Fosbury won gold going over the bar backwards in 1968, and almost every high jumper now copies him.

questions.question: Who won the 5,000m and 10,000m double at both London 2012 and Rio 2016?
questions.explanation: Only one man before him, Finland's Lasse Virén in the 1970s, had won the double at two Games in a row.

questions.question: The Paris 2024 opening ceremony was held mostly on which river?
questions.explanation: The athletes sailed along the river on boats instead of marching into a stadium.

questions.question: How many gold medals did Jesse Owens win at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
questions.explanation: He won the 100m, 200m, long jump and 4x100m relay.

questions.question: Which city became the first to host both the Summer and the Winter Olympics?
questions.explanation: Beijing held the Summer Games in 2008 and the Winter Games in 2022.

questions.question: Which gymnast scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history, in 1976?
questions.explanation: The scoreboard could not show a 10, so it read 1.00 instead.

questions.question: In which year did London host the 'Austerity Games', its second Olympics?
questions.explanation: No new venues were built, and athletes stayed in RAF camps and colleges.

questions.question: Bob Beamon's astonishing long jump at the 1968 Olympics came at altitude in which city?
questions.explanation: He beat the world record by 55 centimetres, with a leap of 8.90 metres.

questions.question: Which two events did Kelly Holmes win at the Athens Olympics in 2004?
questions.explanation: She was 34, and the first Briton to win both since Albert Hill in 1920.

questions.question: Tanni Grey-Thompson won 11 Paralympic gold medals in which sport?
questions.explanation: She also won the London Marathon's wheelchair race six times.

questions.question: Dame Sarah Storey won her first Paralympic medals in 1992, aged 14, in which sport?
questions.explanation: She switched to cycling in 2005 and went on to win many more golds on the bike.

questions.question: Which British sprinter won the 100m at Barcelona 1992, aged 32?
questions.explanation: That made him the oldest Olympic 100m champion by more than four years.

questions.question: Which event, won for Britain by City of London Police officers in 1908 and 1920, was once part of the Olympics?
questions.explanation: Tug of war was dropped after 1920, so the City of London Police are sometimes called the reigning champions.
